title: Braced parameter scan stops at first }: nested ${a:-${b}} is a syntax error
description: lexer/param_scanner.rb takes braced content with [^}]* so any nested expansion terminates early: 'b=inner; echo ${a:-${b}}' errors with exit 2 where dash prints inner; '${a:-${b:-x}}' likewise. POSIX 2.6.2: the matching } is found by counting brace levels, skipping enclosed quoted strings and command substitutions. Fix the scan to track ${ nesting (and the quote/cmd-sub skips), verify the edge matrix differentially: ${a:-${b}}, ${a:-${b:-x}}, ${x#*}} (literal } after close), ${a:-{} (bare { is literal), quoted } inside the word, $(...) with } inside.
close_reason: Fixed in slice 15a: BracedReader + QuotedWord, quoted context threaded scanner->expander; 30-probe dash matrix matches, 24 corpus lines, rake green

title: Lexer state stack for nested case/for/compound contexts

Relevant code: lib/rush/lexer/lex_state.rb, lib/rush/lexer/token_classifier.rb, grammar/shell.y.
acceptance_criteria: Lexer/parser context tracking handles nested for/case/if/while/function constructs inside case bodies and other compound bodies; focused differential corpus includes nested case/for examples; no regressions in alias/reserved-word classification; bundle exec rake is green.

title: Closed stderr must not mask command-not-found/exec failure status
description: Focused architectural review found that diagnostics written after ENOENT/EACCES can raise Errno::EBADF when fd 2 is closed, masking the required POSIX status. Evidence: no-such-rush-xyz 2>&- returns a Ruby stacktrace/status 1 instead of dash's 127; exec no-such-rush-xyz 2>&- returns 1 instead of 127. Relevant code: lib/rush/external.rb error_status, lib/rush/builtins/exec.rb abort_exec, lib/rush/command_runner.rb builtin EBADF handling, lib/rush/fd_entry.rb closed stream.
acceptance_criteria: Diagnostics for external lookup failure and failed exec are best-effort when stderr is closed; no Ruby stacktrace leaks; focused differential cases for no-such 2>&- and exec no-such 2>&- match dash on [stdout, exitstatus]; bundle exec rake is green.
close_reason: External lookup and exec failure diagnostics are now best-effort when fd 2 is closed: EBADF while reporting is swallowed, preserving 127/126 status and preventing stack traces. Added unit and dash differential cases for closed stderr; full rake green.

title: exec redirect-only permanence (exec >file / 3>file / 2>&1 persist)
description:
Last path-2 piece (M5). exec with only redirects (no command word) must apply them permanently to the shell IO table for the rest of the session.

Root cause already diagnosed: Executor#with_redirects ensure closes the file opened over base (io.ios - base.ios), undoing exec's replace_io. The dup case (exec 2>&1) already works because no new stream is opened.

Fix: skip the close when the executor committed the io (io.equal?(@io) after replace_io). Verify bit-exact vs dash: exec >f / 3>f / 2>&1 / 9<f persist; subshell isolation (( exec >f ); after) does not leak; bad-path exec already fatal (7aj). One slice, green rake.
close_reason: exec redirect-only permanence: with_redirects skips closing the io exec committed via replace_io (io.equal?(@io)); verified vs dash + corpus + unit test; green rake, 100% cov

title: function-call redirects not applied to the function body
description: `f(){ echo body; }; f >file` — dash sends body to file; rush prints body to stdout. CommandRunner#run_function does not thread the redirected io into the function body (dispatch passes io to builtin/External but run_function ignores it). Likely fix: run the function body under executor.with_io(io). Found by the 7aj redirect fuzz; orthogonal to 7aj. Verify bit-exact vs dash + add to differential corpus.
close_reason: run_function now binds the call's redirect io to the body via with_io, but only when a redirect layered a new table (io != base) so exec inside a no-redirect call still persists; verified vs dash incl. exec-scope cases + corpus + unit; green rake 100% cov

title: Subshell job-table knowledge per POSIX 2.12: keep the async pids for display (jobs, $(jobs -p)) while waitability resets
description: Re-adjudicated 2026-07-11 against POSIX.1-2017 directly (project rule: where dash diverges from the standard, the standard wins). The normative basis is NOT "match dash" — it is 2.12 verbatim: the shell execution environment includes "Process IDs of the last commands in asynchronous lists known to this shell environment", and "A subshell environment shall be created as a duplicate of the shell environment" — so async-pid knowledge duplicates into every subshell environment. The wait page carves waitability out normatively ("The known process IDs are applicable only for invocations of wait in the current shell execution environment"), and the jobs APPLICATION USAGE blesses $(jobs -p) as THE portable way to refer to jobs. Probe matrix (2026-07-11, dash 0.5.x / bash / rush HEAD c86ffea): [C] jobs | cat — dash and bash both list, rush prints nothing (pipeline stages are subshell environments per 2.12; either reading, duplicate or current-env extension, requires listing) — rush bug. [E] sh -c "sleep 0.4; exit 7" & wait $(jobs -p) — dash rc=7, bash rc=7, rush rc=0 via empty substitution — rush breaks the POSIX-blessed idiom; bash proves it needs only a table copy, NOT the dash no-fork trick (rush-mv8.7, now closed). [F] forked (wait $!) — unanimous rc=127, rush already standard-correct; nothing to do. [B] (jobs; echo x); echo tail — ALL THREE print nothing: the original claim here that dash subshells list the parent table is FALSE (only pipeline stages do; dash EV_EXIT masked the earlier probe). Strict 2.12 letter says the pids are known even there; both oracles print nothing, so keep (jobs) shapes out of the differential corpus and decide: the clean conforming design is one read-only copy in EVERY subshell environment (uniform, more consistent than either oracle), with waitability/%kill reset as today. Best bundled with the jobs rendering seam (command-text column already landed in mv8.6).
acceptance_criteria: wait $(jobs -p) returns the job status (probe E: rc=7 like dash and bash); jobs | cat lists the parent jobs under and without -m (corpus lines); forked (wait $!) stays 127; full rake green.
close_reason: Uniform POSIX 2.12 display copy: enter_subshell demotes entries to inherited copies — listable by jobs/jobs -p (wait $(jobs -p) returns rc=7 like both oracles), refused by wait/%id/reaping. 7 corpus lines pin the dash-agreeing shapes; probe matrix byte-for-byte; rake green (2256); pty smoke green.

title: Container-only failure: inherited-fd writes reordered in real_shell_spec (pre-existing)
description:
In the rush-test Docker container (ruby:4.0.5-slim, Debian) two real_shell_spec examples fail deterministically while passing natively: 'redirects to a parent-inherited fd and leaves it open for later commands' expects one
two but gets two

title: Centralize child reaping: one waitpid owner consulted by synchronous waits
description: The epic's flagged design risk, resolved first while everything is still terminal-free. Today PipelineRunner/BackgroundRunner (and the wait builtin path) each call waitpid2 directly; once a SIGCHLD/WUNTRACED reaper exists it would steal their statuses. Refactor so exactly one owner performs every waitpid — the job-table layer — and synchronous waits become queries against it (block until the owner has reaped that pid). Pure Ruby-VM refactor: no process groups, no tty, fully testable with FakeSystemCalls; behaviour must be corpus-invariant (dash differential unchanged).
acceptance_criteria: All waitpid2/waitpid call sites in lib/ live in the single reaping owner; PipelineRunner/BackgroundRunner/wait consult it; full bundle exec rake green; differential corpus unchanged.
close_reason: Already satisfied by the phase-5 terminal-free half (rush-iwh): JobTable declares and implements single reaping ownership — the only waitpid2 call sites in lib/ are the SystemCalls seam and JobTable#reap_one/#poll; every synchronous wait routes through jobs.await (external.rb:21, command_substitution.rb:55, subshell_runner.rb:20, pipeline_runner.rb:144) or jobs.wait_for/wait_all (wait builtin); foreign statuses are stashed, background statuses filed on their entries. Verified by grep audit 2026-07-10.

title: wait builtin: centralized child reaping (JobTable) + pid operands per POSIX
description:
Mandatory-POSIX gap: rush has no wait builtin at all (rush: wait: not found, 127) — wait is core XCU, not a UP job-control option. Also resolves rush-mv8's recorded design risk (waitpid ownership) as its standalone first slice: a JobTable becomes the single owner of child reaping; all synchronous waits (External, PipelineRunner, SubshellRunner, CommandSubstitution) route through JobTable#await(pid), which consults a stash and loops waitpid2(-1), stashing foreign statuses by pid. Side effect: background zombies get reaped whenever any foreground wait completes.

Oracle findings (dash, no pty needed): wait no-args reaps all known bg pids, returns 0. wait pid... returns last operand's status; unknown pid => 127 (incl. wait 0); repeated wait on a reaped pid returns the remembered status again (statuses are remembered indefinitely); killed child => 128+sig (137 for KILL); non-numeric operand => 'Illegal number: X' status 2, leading dash => 'Illegal option' status 2, > INT32_MAX => Illegal number. Subshell: live inherited pid => ECHILD => status 0 (dash behaviour); already-remembered => remembered status; unknown => 127 — waitpid(-1) routing during fg waits is exactly what makes the remembered-in-subshell case match dash.

Out of scope: %job operands (rush-mv8 slice 2 — dash resolves %1 even without set -m; divergence documented until then); async-list stdin /dev/null and bg SIGINT/SIGQUIT ignore (separate beads).
acceptance_criteria: bundle exec rake fully green; differential corpus lines covering: wait no-args, wait $! (exit/false/kill -9), repeated wait on same pid, unknown pid 127, illegal number 2, multiple pids last-status, subshell cases
close_reason: Landed as Phase 5 (Slice 11a): JobTable centralizes reaping, wait builtin dash/POSIX-verified, rake green

title: Backslash-newline line continuation unsupported (misparse; IndexError crash after &&)

Found by the phase-4 startup slice via real files: /etc/profile.d/locale.sh (export list continued across lines misparses, "LC_MESSAGES: not found") and gawk.sh (the && continuation crash). Likely belongs in the lexer line-feed path shared with ProgramReader continuations. Add a crash regression spec plus differential corpus lines.

title: Slice: interactive error and EOF semantics per POSIX 2.8.1
description: Audit the POSIX 2.8.1 "Consequences of Shell Errors" interactive column: expansion errors, redirection errors, command-not-found and special-builtin failures must return to the prompt, not exit the shell; EOF (Ctrl-D) exits. Repl already resumes on ParseError/ExpansionError/ReadonlyError/BuiltinError — verify the full table and pin behaviour differentially with dash -i reading a piped script ([stdout, exitstatus] stays comparable; prompts land on ignored stderr).

title: Slice: interactive signal handling (SIGINT re-prompts; ignore SIGQUIT/SIGTERM)
description: Interactive shells must survive signals: ignore SIGTERM and SIGQUIT while interactive; SIGINT at the prompt discards the current line and re-prompts instead of killing the shell; SIGINT during a foreground command returns to the prompt after the child dies. User traps (trap builtin) override the interactive defaults where POSIX allows. Children must get default dispositions restored before exec. Ruby caveat: trap handlers run deferred on the main thread at VM safe points — keep handler bodies trivial.

title: RedirectScope must close overwritten owned redirection streams
description: Executor#with_redirects folds redirects into a final IoTable and cleanup closes only entries present in that final table but absent from base. If a redirect opens an owned stream and a later redirect overwrites the fd (e.g. : >f 1>&2 or exec >f 1>&2), the opened entry can be lost until GC/process exit. Relevant code: lib/rush/executor.rb with_redirects/close_redirect_io, lib/rush/io_table.rb close_opened_over, redirection file/heredoc appliers.

title: off-tty set -m: a signal-stopped pipeline stage hangs rush forever (stage supervisor waits non-WUNTRACED)
description: Probed 2026-07-11 while adjudicating rush-mv8.7. Shape: set -m; sh -c "exit 5" | sh -c "kill -TSTP $$"; echo st:$? — rush blocks forever (two orphaned probe pairs sat 7h in do_wait: parent rush -> stage supervisor -> sh in state T). Oracles do NOT hang on this bare form: dash answers st:148 (128+TSTP, job parks Stopped), bash answers st:133. The mechanism is the recorded mv8.4 journal note: the stage supervisor (the extra fork layer dash EV_EXIT-execs away) waits non-WUNTRACED, so a stopped grandchild never settles. Journal claimed dash with a brace-wrapped stage would block the same way — probing falsifies that for dash ({ sh -c "kill -TSTP $$"; } still st:148, EV_EXIT reaches through braces), though bash DOES hang on the wrapped form. No reading of POSIX permits an indefinite hang where both oracles return 128+n and park the job Stopped; per the project rule (standard beats oracle) this is a rush bug regardless of the corpus never exercising the shape. A real-world trigger needs no TSTP tricks: kill -STOP aimed at a pipeline member of any set -m script wedges the whole script. Fix direction is free: supervisor waits WUNTRACED and propagates the stop (self-SIGSTOP, CONT relay), or EV_EXIT-execs simple external stages away (the closed rush-mv8.7 optimization would also dissolve the layer).
acceptance_criteria: set -m; sh -c "exit 5" | sh -c "kill -TSTP $$"; echo st:$? returns promptly with the job parked Stopped (dash oracle: st:148); kill -STOP of a stage from outside does not wedge the shell; full rake green.

title: Job control: set -m, jobs/fg/bg, process groups, terminal control
description: The half of the original phase 4 that steps OUTSIDE the Ruby-VM platform; Unix-only by OS physics (Windows has no POSIX process groups, no SIGTSTP/SIGCONT, no controlling terminal), so it ships behind a platform gate ("job control not supported" elsewhere). Scope: set -m; jobs/fg/bg builtins; %job ids in wait and kill; job table with Running/Stopped/Done states and pre-prompt notifications; one process group per pipeline (double setpgid in parent and child); WUNTRACED waits with stopped-child state threaded through Status; terminal handover via tcsetpgrp — decided approach: IO#ioctl (core Ruby) with per-platform TIOCSPGRP constants keyed on RbConfig::CONFIG["host_os"] (Linux asm-generic 0x5410; darwin/BSD 0x80047476), Fiddle-into-libc as fallback; ignore SIGTTOU around the call. DESIGN RISK to resolve before unfreezing: waitpid ownership — a SIGCHLD self-pipe reaper doing waitpid(-1, WNOHANG|WUNTRACED) steals statuses from the synchronous waitpid2 calls in PipelineRunner/BackgroundRunner; all child reaping must be centralized into one owner (job table the synchronous waits consult) as the FIRST slice. Testing: FakeSystemCalls grows a mini process-group/tty model for deterministic specs; real behaviour via pty smokes in the Docker gate; the dash oracle is only meaningful under a pty.
notes: RESCOPED to the terminal half only: set -m, process groups (double setpgid), tcsetpgrp via IO#ioctl (TIOCSPGRP+TIOCGPGRP, per-host_os constants), WUNTRACED + Stopped state, SIGTSTP, working fg/bg, pre-prompt notifications (dash prints none off-tty — probed), and the jobs command-text column (dash keeps text only under a tty; consider commandtext-style AST rendering then). Everything terminal-free landed via rush-iwh (wait+JobTable) and rush-rg2 (subshell clearing, jobs, %ids, fg/bg stubs). Unfrozen 2026-07-10, decomposed into rush-mv8.1..7. mv8.1 closed by audit (phase-5 JobTable already the single waitpid owner — no SIGCHLD reaper ever needed; notifications can poll WNOHANG at prompt time like dash's showjobs; WUNTRACED is a flag change in JobTable#reap_one). mv8.2 landed off-tty monitor (groups, TSTP ignore, $- m, corpus-pinned). mv8.3 landed the terminal: Terminal.acquire = dash setjobctl(1) (open /dev/tty or dup'd std tty fd, tcgetpgrp + TTIN wait loop, remember initial, setpgid(0,0), take tty), tcgetpgrp/tcsetpgrp on IO#ioctl (Linux 0x540F/0x5410, BSD 0x40047477/0x80047476; unknown Unix degrades to grouping-only — Fiddle fallback deliberately not taken), TTOU held SIG_IGN around the ioctl, handover child-side in grouped_child + parent-side via JobControl#foreground (covers spawn path), reclaim in ensure after every fg wait; -i now defaults -m (dash mflag=iflag, probed smi); with tty: TSTP+TTOU base-ignored, TTIN stays default (probed — it parks a bg-started shell); set +m restores dispositions, gives tty back to initial owner, rejoins it. Durable state: JobTable::Control (root bit + terminal). Proof: docker/job-control-smoke.rb — differential pty smoke, rush picture == dash picture. Probing lesson: orphaned pgrps discard stop signals — wrap probes in sh -c. Slice order next: .4 WUNTRACED/SIGTSTP -> .5 fg/bg -> .6 notifications.
close_reason: Epic complete: the terminal half of job control is dash 0.5.13-equivalent. Landed across slices 13a-13e (commits d506f45, c96473b, 130bbec, aa7ae7b, bfef010): set -m with monitor default for interactive shells; one process group per job (double setpgid + spawn pgroup); tcsetpgrp terminal handover via IO#ioctl (child- and parent-side, SIGTTOU held ignored) with dash's full setjobctl acquisition dance; WUNTRACED waits with the Stopped state threaded through Status/Job/JobTable (^Z parks whole jobs, wait answers 148 repeatably, exit refused once via the job_warning window); working fg/bg (SIGCONT + reattachment + per-job jobctl refusal bit); pre-prompt notifications and the cmdtxt command-text column, byte-for-byte dash. Proof: 72-line differential job-control corpus + the differential pty smoke (rush -i vs dash -i, extracted-picture equality) in the Docker gate; full rake green at every slice. The recorded design risk (waitpid ownership) had already dissolved into the phase-5 single-owner JobTable. rush-mv8.7 (EV_EXIT no-fork) detached as a standalone deferred P4 with its divergence list; follow-ups filed along the way: rush-erq (container fd ordering, pre-existing), rush-r6i (jobs listing in forked children), rush-hkp (printsignal).

title: Honour parent-inherited fds in >&n / <&n redirections (dash-compat)
description: rush resolves a redirection's source fd in n>&m / n<&m only against its own IoTable (fds 0/1/2 plus those opened in-shell via exec). An fd >= 3 inherited open from the parent process is invisible, so 'true >&9' with fd 9 inherited-open raises RedirectError -> status 2, where dash dups the real OS fd and succeeds (0). POSIX and dash operate on the actual process fd table. Goal: make >&n / <&n fall back to the real inherited fd when n is not tracked by the IoTable, matching dash.
design: IoTable currently abstracts logical fds -> IO objects and is the boundary for redirects and child-spawn fd setup. To honour inherited fds, when n is absent from the table, probe the real OS fd (e.g. IO.for_fd(n) guarded by a fcntl F_GETFD / rescue Errno::EBADF) and dup from it instead of erroring; a genuinely-closed fd must still error like dash. Open design question: whether raw OS fds should leak through the IoTable abstraction, and how this interacts with subshell/child fd inheritance and close_redirect bookkeeping.
acceptance_criteria: exec 9>/dev/null; true >&9; echo $?  -> 0 (matches dash); an inherited-open fd works as a redirect source/target; a genuinely-closed fd still errors (status 2). Add specs that control fd state explicitly (the differential harness deliberately closes inherited fds per rush-7ue, so cover this with targeted unit/integration specs rather than ambient-fd differential cases).
close_reason: Implemented inherited fd probing for dup redirects: absent source fds now fall back to a non-owning IO.for_fd wrapper, while logically closed fds still fail. Added fake-system unit coverage and real subprocess specs with explicit fd 9 inheritance/closure.

title: fd-facing test primaries (-t, -p via /dev/stdin) see the interpreter's real fds, not shell redirections
description: [ -t 1 ] >/dev/null still reports a tty on a pty (dash: 1), and echo x | { [ -p /dev/stdin ]; } misses the pipe: builtins run in-process and apply redirections through IoTable rather than dup2, so anything that inspects real process fds (tty_fd?, /dev/fd/N paths) is blind to shell-level redirects. Invisible in the differential harness (all fds are pipes there). Found by the slice-15b adversarial verifier. The honest fix is the real-fd model — see docs/architecture/pipeline-fd.md postscript; this bead is the concrete symptom to re-probe if that migration reopens.

title: EV_EXIT-style no-fork for tail subshells and single-builtin command substitutions
description: Parked optimization from the epic notes: avoid the extra fork for tail subshells and single-builtin command substitutions (dash's EV_EXIT), restoring the POSIX-blessed 'wait $(jobs -p)' idiom (jobs must run in the current shell there). Not required for core job control; revisit after rush-mv8.6.
acceptance_criteria: wait $(jobs -p) waits for the running background jobs like dash; no behaviour regression in the corpus; full rake green.
notes: Formerly parked inside epic rush-mv8 (closed 2026-07-11). Standalone deferred optimization: dash execs a tail-position command in place (EV_EXIT), which rush's extra fork layer diverges from in three recorded ways: (1) pipeline-stage pids/self-$$-signals (journal, mv8.4: off-tty pipeline stops), (2) wait $(jobs -p) yields nothing (phase-5 note), (3) jobs-in-forked-children listing (rush-r6i). Landing it would also collapse those divergences.
close_reason: Adjudicated against POSIX per the standard-beats-oracle rule (probes 2026-07-11). Every standard-visible behavior EV_EXIT would restore is either dash diverging from POSIX subshell semantics — tail-position (wait $!) leaking main-shell waitability, where bash agrees with rush 127 and 2.12+wait side with rush — or belongs to a behavioral bead that does not need no-fork: wait $(jobs -p) works in bash via a job-table copy (rush-r6i, rescoped onto 2.12), and the stopped-stage supervisor hang is filed as rush-l4o. What remains here is a pure fork-count optimization; the project goal is the standard, not dash process topology.

title: Backslash-newline inside operators (&\<newline>& should join to &&)
description: dash splices line continuations at the character-read level, so a backslash-newline INSIDE an operator joins it: `true &\<newline>& echo hi` runs echo. rush (slice 10g) removes continuations between tokens, inside words, double quotes and heredoc data, but the operator matcher does not see through the pair, so the split-operator form tokenizes as two operators. Pathological input, real implementation cost (character-level splice under the whole scanner); deliberately deferred — documented in docs/journal.md.
close_reason: Operator matcher and IO_NUMBER lookahead now see through backslash-newline pairs; dash parity verified (unit, differential corpus, 300-program fuzz)

title: rush >&n / <&n does not honour fds inherited from the parent process
description: Redirect duplication (n>&m, n<&m) resolves the source fd only against rush's own IoTable (0/1/2 plus fds opened in-shell via exec). An fd >= 3 inherited open from the parent is invisible, so 'true >&9' with fd 9 inherited-open errors (status 2) where dash dups the real fd and succeeds (0). POSIX/dash use the real OS fd table. Low priority: scripts rarely rely on inherited high fds, and the differential harness now closes them. Documenting the divergence.
